priority.override_reason: Fresh ranks 1 through 5 remain closed by the documented scheduler/direct-leaf, hash-map, typed object-field, numeric ownership, constructor-receiver, and RegExp rejection evidence. The rank-6 CDJS receipt instead exposes 1,151 of 1,169 main-thread samples in the generic call_callee_with_marker -> call_function -> eval_function_bytecode chain. Its drawMotionOnVoxelMap body creates ordinary nested closures over slot-backed locals, so the existing direct-slot P0 mechanism stops precisely at a structural eligibility boundary rather than a previously rejected leaf specialization. The independent rank-17 JetStream AES profile is deliberately a control, not fabricated shared-target evidence: it already spends its hot execution on direct leaves. This unit removes only the ordinary captured-closure boundary while retaining every dynamic, class, lexical-this, arguments, eval, with, and super exclusion.

mechanism.summary: Permit a slot-backed direct call to create ordinary non-lexical-this function closures, promoting its local-upvalue vector lazily on the first actual capture so sibling and escaping closures retain the same cells as the generic frame.
mechanism.generality: Admission is compiled-opcode classification only: every Op::NewFunction with lexical_this false is compatible, while Op::NewClass and any lexical-this function literal remain incompatible. It has no workload, source-path, checksum, function-name, iteration-count, input-size, result, or benchmark condition. Existing direct-call exclusions for arguments, direct eval, with, super, generators, async functions, named-function bindings, dynamic bindings, and non-seedable parameters remain unchanged.
semantic_risks: preserving one shared cell for all sibling closures and the declaring frame after a local is promoted
preserving escaped closure lifetime after the slot-backed parent frame returns
preserving per-iteration lexical environments when a loop binding is captured
preserving received upvalues, TDZ markers, and writes made before or after capture
retaining generic-frame behavior for class creation, lexical-this closures, arguments, direct eval, with, and super
